newsitem.title: CHINA: Individual forex trade booming at Shanghai bank.
newsitem.headline: Individual forex trade booming at Shanghai bank.

text.p: Individual foreign exchange transactions at the Shanghai branch of the Bank of Communications have boomed since it opened a telephone trading service and evening market earlier this year, Business News said on Friday.
Trading value surpassed $110 million in the first half of 1997, up 400 percent from the same 1996 period, the newspaper said.
Of that amount, $53 million was traded over the counter and $61 million by phone, it said. It gave no further details.
Foreign exchange transactions were first opened to individuals in Shanghai in 1993, official media has said.
Investors can trade Japanese yen, Deutsche marks, French francs, Swiss francs, and U.S., Canadian, Hong Kong and Australian dollars, it has said.
At present, foreign currency trading by individual investors is limited to spot trading, and futures trading is prohibited, it has said.

The Shanghai branch of the Bank of Communications was one of five commercial banks in Shanghai providing foreign currency trading for individuals, the Business News said, adding it was also the busiest.
